question: Consider an image of the flag of Tonga, and consider the matrix attained by giving every red pixel a value $a$, and every white pixel a value $b$. What is the maximal possible rank of this matrix?

7.text:
The flag of Tonga consists of a solid red field containing a white canton (upper hoist), within which is centered a red Greek cross. Treating the flag as a pixel matrix therefore yields an all-\(a\) matrix modified by a 0-1 pattern \(W\) whose 1-entries occupy precisely the white regions. Those white regions comprise exactly four rectangles (the four rectangular “panes” lying between the arms of the cross and the edges of the canton).  

Each rectangular indicator is an outer product of two 0-1 vectors and hence has rank 1, so  
\[
W=\sum_{i=1}^4 R_i,\qquad\operatorname{rank}(W)\le4.
\]  
The full matrix may be rewritten  
\[
M=aJ+(b-a)W,
\]  
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix (rank 1). Consequently  
\[
M\text{ lies in a vector space spanned by at most five rank-1 matrices,}
\]  
which implies \(\operatorname{rank}(M)\le5\).  

For generic numerical values \(a\neq b\) and for pixel resolutions in which the four white rectangles occupy linearly independent sets of rows and columns, the five rank-1 summands are themselves linearly independent; the bound 5 is therefore attained. No larger rank is possible, because the geometry of the Tongan flag never generates more than four white rectangles.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: 5 (four white rectangles give rank(W)≤4; adding the all-red background contributes one more dimension)

The associated matrix \(M\) therefore takes the constant value \(a\) everywhere except on the white regions (the canton excluding the cross), where it takes the constant value \(b\).

This admits the decomposition
\[
M = a\,J + (b-a)\,I,
\]
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix (rank 1) and \(I\) is the 0-1 indicator of the white regions. Consequently

The support of \(I\) consists of exactly four axis-aligned rectangles lying inside the canton (the regions lying above, below, to the left, and to the right of the cross). Each such rectangle indicator is itself a rank-1 matrix—the outer product of the indicator vector of its row interval with the indicator vector of its column interval. Hence \(I\) is a sum of four rank-1 matrices, which implies
\[
\rank(I)\le 4
\]
and therefore
\[
\rank(M)\le 5.
\]
For generic choices \(a\neq b\) and for pixel resolutions fine enough to realize the four rectangles as nonempty and in general position, the five summands are linearly independent, so the bound 5 is attained.

Thus the maximal possible rank is 5.
